newsitem.title: FRANCE: Elf Atochem buys Laporte's adhesives operation.
newsitem.headline: Elf Atochem buys Laporte's adhesives operation.

text.p: Elf Atochem, the chemicals unit of French oil group Elf Aquitaine, said on Thursday it had agreed to buy the European adhesives and sealants activities of British specialty chemicals group Laporte Plc.

The activities represent turnover of 100 million pounds ($167 million) and include Evode and Sovereign in Britain, Evode Industries in Ireland, Simson in the Netherlands and Hey'di in Germany. It gave no details on the price of the deal.
The acquisition is part of Elf Atochem's expansion strategy in speciality chemicals, the company said.
The operations will be integrated into AtoFindlay, a company set up in January 1996 after the acquisition of Findlay Adhesives of the United States.

Addition of the new activities will give AtoFindlay turnover in 1997 of three billion francs and will consolidate its position as one of the world's leading adhesives manufacturers, the statement said.
Under chief executive Jim Leng, Luton-based Laporte has embarked on a string of non-core asset disposals since announcing plans for a major overhaul at the end of 1995.
Leng said in September that the company had raised 60 million pounds through sell-offs in the first nine months, with around 20 million pounds' worth of businesses left to be sold. ($1=.5977 Pound)
